slides.title: Recursion & Call Stack Structure
slides.prompt: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself. Every call pushes a new stack frame (containing parameters and local variables) onto the execution stack until a base case stops recursion.

slides.title: Base Case Identification
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing check condition that halts recursion.

slides.title: Stack Overflow Root Cause
slides.prompt: What causes a Stack Overflow error during recursive function execution?
options: Exceeding allocated call stack memory due to missing or unreachable base cases
Dereferencing a nullptr inside the loop
Allocating too much memory on the dynamic heap
Buffer overflow in C-style string buffers
slides.correctAnswer: Exceeding allocated call stack memory due to missing or unreachable base cases

slides.title: Tail Recursion Concept
slides.prompt: In tail recursion, the recursive call is the ___ statement executed in the function.

slides.title: Tail Call Optimization (TCO)
slides.prompt: What does Tail Call Optimization (TCO) perform under compiler optimization?
options: Replaces the recursive call stack frame reuse like an iterative loop to save stack space
Converts recursive calls to multi-threaded tasks
Moves recursive variables to dynamic heap memory
slides.correctAnswer: Replaces the recursive call stack frame reuse like an iterative loop to save stack space

options: Function A calls Function B, which in turn calls Function A
A function calling itself directly in a loop
